body.zh-HK:
> 面試官問：「你怎樣把簡單工作交給較小模型，把複雜工作交給較強模型，而不讓 routing 變成另一個不可解釋的風險？」
>
> 答啱一半嘅答案：「難題全部送去最大模型，其他送小模型。」

## Routing 是一個有後果的決定器

Model routing 不只是省錢的 if statement。它先要定義工作類型和 output contract：是抽取欄位、把已核實資料改寫成草稿、比對兩段文字，還是回答缺少來源的問題？再看輸入完整度、格式、語言、長度、錯誤代價、延遲預算和是否需要 human review。若 router 不能判斷，或下游模型 timeout、輸出不合 schema、沒有足夠證據，系統不能默默假裝成功。它要回退到較簡單、較受約束的路徑，或建立明確 handoff。

一條好 route policy 是可讀的。例子：有固定 schema 且內容完整的 fixture 先走 deterministic validator；合格才走小模型作分類；輸入含衝突、缺欄位、超出長度預算或需要引用的 case，改交 review queue，而不是盲目升級到大模型。較強模型可以是候選 route，但它也有成本、延遲、資料處理和輸出不穩定的代價。每次 route 應留下 reason code，而不是只留下一個最終答案。

## 服務櫃位不是失敗，是 fallback

機場不會把所有旅客送進同一條通道。拿著完整登機證的人走自助閘；證件不完整或行程有問題的人去服務櫃位。服務櫃位不是失敗，而是把不確定情況交給能處理的人。Model fallback 也是這樣：不確定時保住邊界，比假裝最強模型一定救到更可靠。

## 答題時要交代嘅判斷

由 failure mode 出發，而不是由模型名字出發。為每一個 route 寫清楚 allowed input、預期輸出、time/cost budget、hard failures 和 fallback target。比較時看 task success、schema validity、source sufficiency、latency、cost 和人工接手量，而不是只看平均 quality。把 router 自己當成要評估的 component：route 錯了的 case，可能比小模型答錯更難發現。

## 答案何時會太薄

「大模型是 fallback」不是完整設計。最小 baseline 可以是 single route：先做 deterministic validation，再產生草稿，所有不完整 case 交人。只有當固定 evaluation 顯示不同工作真的有可重複差異，才加第二條 route。若新增 router 只是為了炫耀多模型架構，維護成本很可能高過收益。

## 技術證據

提供 `routing-policy.yaml`、輸入 contract、route reason code enum、static request/response fixture、schema validator、timeout test、fallback test、trace sample 和一個 `route-eval.jsonl`。將模型 ID、設定、prompt version、tool permission 和 evaluation version 同一筆 trace 記錄。若使用 demo model，只放無 key 的靜態 fixture；不要用 mock 成功輸出暗示真的呼叫過服務。

## 交付、業務與風險證據

`handoff-policy.md` 要寫明哪位 reviewer 接哪類 failure、何時不可以自動重試、輸出只可當草稿還是可作排序、以及 cost／latency 上限由誰擁有。Release note 應列出 route 改動、固定 case 的 Evidence Delta 和 rollback 路徑。不要把較低平均 cost 寫成已實現節省，也不要把 fallback 說成已處理所有風險。

## 延伸閱讀

[Language model family 點揀](/zh-HK/articles/language-model-families-and-when-to-use-them)、[LLM eval、human review 與 observability](/zh-HK/articles/llm-evals-human-review-and-observability) 和 [Agent workflow 不只評 final answer](/zh-HK/articles/evaluate-an-ai-agent-workflow-not-just-the-final-answer)。

## 範圍說明

這是 AI.DOG 的單題練習。route、模型、資料、trace 和成本均為虛構教學草稿；沒有連接服務、沒有 API key、沒有真實機構 workflow 或已完成的業務成效。

>
> 答对一半的答案：“难题全部送去最大模型，其他送小模型。”

Model routing 不只是省钱的 if statement。它先要定义工作类型和 output contract：是抽取字段、把已核实数据改写成草稿、比对两段文字，还是回答缺少来源的问题？再看输入完整度、格式、语言、长度、错误代价、延迟预算和是否需要 human review。若 router 不能判断，或下游模型 timeout、输出不合 schema、没有足够证据，系统不能默默假装成功。它要退回较简单、较受约束的路径，或建立明确 handoff。

从 failure mode 出发，而不是从模型名称出发。为每个 route 写清楚 allowed input、预期输出、time/cost budget、hard failures 和 fallback target。比较时看 task success、schema validity、source sufficiency、latency、cost 与人工接手量，而不是只看平均 quality。把 router 本身当成要评估的 component：route 错了的 case，可能比小模型答错更难发现。

`handoff-policy.md` 要写清楚哪位 reviewer 接哪类 failure、何时不可以自动重试、输出只能当草稿还是可用于排序，以及 cost／latency 上限由谁拥有。Release note 应列出 route 改动、固定 case 的 Evidence Delta 和 rollback 路径。不要把较低平均 cost 写成已经实现节省，也不要把 fallback 说成已经处理所有风险。

body.en:
> Interviewer asks: “How would you send simple work to a smaller model and harder work to a stronger model without turning routing into another opaque risk?”
>
> Half-right answer: “Send every hard question to the biggest model and everything else to the small one.”

## Routing is a decision-maker with consequences

Model routing is not merely a cost-saving if statement. First define the task and output contract: is the work extracting fields, rewriting verified material into a draft, comparing two passages, or answering a question with missing sources? Then consider input completeness, format, language, length, error cost, latency budget, and the need for human review. If a router cannot decide, or a downstream model times out, violates the schema, or lacks sufficient evidence, the system cannot silently pretend it succeeded. It must fall back to a simpler, more constrained path or create an explicit handoff.

A good route policy is readable. For example, a complete fixture with a fixed schema first passes a deterministic validator; only then can a small model classify it. A case with conflict, missing fields, excess length, or citation need goes to a review queue instead of blindly escalating to a larger model. A stronger model can be a candidate route, but it also carries cost, latency, data-handling, and output-variability trade-offs. Record a reason code for every route, not only a final answer.

## A service desk is a fallback, not a failure

An airport does not send every passenger through one lane. Someone with a complete boarding pass can use a self-service gate; missing documents or an unusual itinerary go to a service desk. The desk is not failure. It is a place for uncertainty to reach someone equipped to handle it. A model fallback works the same way: holding the boundary under uncertainty is more reliable than pretending the strongest model always rescues the case.

## The judgement an interviewer is listening for

Start with failure modes, not model names. For each route, state the allowed input, expected output, time and cost budget, hard failures, and fallback target. Compare task success, schema validity, source sufficiency, latency, cost, and human handoff volume, not average quality alone. Treat the router itself as an evaluated component: a wrongly routed case can be harder to spot than a small model's wrong answer.

## Where an answer goes thin

“A large model is the fallback” is not a design. The smallest baseline can be one route: deterministic validation, then a draft, with all incomplete cases handed to a person. Add a second route only when fixed evaluation demonstrates a repeatable difference between task types. If a router exists only to showcase a multi-model architecture, its maintenance cost may exceed its benefit.

## Technical evidence

Provide `routing-policy.yaml`, an input contract, a route-reason-code enum, static request and response fixtures, a schema validator, timeout test, fallback test, trace sample, and `route-eval.jsonl`. Store model ID, configuration, prompt version, tool permission, and evaluation version in the same trace. For a demo model, keep no-key static fixtures only; do not use a mock success response to imply a real service call happened.

## Delivery, business, and risk evidence

`handoff-policy.md` should state which reviewer receives which failure, when automatic retry is forbidden, whether output is draft-only or ranking support, and who owns cost and latency limits. A release note should list route changes, Evidence Delta on fixed cases, and a rollback path. Do not write lower average cost as realised savings or imply that a fallback solves every risk.

## Further reading

[Choose a language-model family](/en/articles/language-model-families-and-when-to-use-them), [LLM evaluation, human review, and observability](/en/articles/llm-evals-human-review-and-observability), and [evaluate an agent workflow, not only its final answer](/en/articles/evaluate-an-ai-agent-workflow-not-just-the-final-answer).

## Scope note

This is an AI.DOG single-question practice exercise. Routes, models, data, traces, and costs are fictional teaching-draft material. No service is connected, no API key is used, and it describes no real organisation workflow or achieved business outcome.
